annotation_description: Played Breeding Pool on turn 2 when Botanical Sanctum would enter untapped for free (only 1 other land, meeting the ≤2 condition). Breeding Pool either costs 2 life to enter untapped or enters tapped, while Botanical Sanctum produces the same colors (G/U) and enters untapped with no cost. Botanical Sanctum should be played now while the condition is met, saving Breeding Pool for later turns when there may be 3+ other lands and Botanical Sanctum would enter tapped.

Casting Badgermole Cub instead of Llanowar Elves on turn 2 delays the ability to cast Appa, Steadfast Guardian on turn 3. With Llanowar Elves (1 mana), the player would have 4 mana on turn 3 (3 lands + elf), enabling a turn 3 Appa by playing Hallowed Fountain untapped. Additionally, having Llanowar Elves on board first would synergize with Badgermole Cub's 'whenever you tap a creature for mana, add {G}' ability when Cub is cast later.

After Ouroboroid's combat trigger, Ouroboroid is 2/4 and Gene Pollinator is 2/3. Both creatures can profitably attack into the opponent's 2/2 Badgermole Cubs and 1/1 Llanowar Elves - they survive any single block. Ouroboroid in particular should be attacking since it's growing exponentially and forcing the opponent to trade resources favorably.

Cast Doc Aurlock before playing Hushwood Verge land drop. Should play the land first to maximize available mana and options. Additionally, with Ouroboroid threatening to grow exponentially on the opponent's side, holding up Appa (which has flash) to flash in on opponent's turn to airbend key permanents and create blockers may have been stronger than deploying Doc Aurlock, which has limited immediate impact without exile/graveyard synergies set up.

annotation_description: Appa's ETB allows airbending 'any number' of nonland permanents. The player only selected one Badgermole Cub instead of selecting both Badgermole Cubs (and possibly Llanowar Elves). Airbending both Cubs would allow recasting them from exile for {2} each (or free with Doc Aurlock's cost reduction), triggering Appa's token generation for each spell cast from exile AND re-triggering the Cubs' earthbend ETB abilities. The player had Doc Aurlock in hand which would make exile casts cost {2} less, meaning the Cubs could be recast for free. This represents significant missed value - multiple Ally tokens and multiple earthbend triggers.

At 6 life, paying 2 life to play Temple Garden untapped from exile is very costly, dropping to 4 life. The Temple Garden from exile was likely playable via Interdimensional Web Watch's exile effect. Meanwhile, the player already has 5 lands on the battlefield plus Llanowar Elves for mana. Paying 2 life when already at critically low life total is dangerous, especially when the opponent has an established board with multiple creatures. The player should have either let Temple Garden enter tapped (saving 2 life) or prioritized casting Doc Aurlock, Grizzled Genius first and playing the land tapped, since mana wasn't likely the bottleneck this turn with the existing mana base.
